resources.string: Laryngeal inlet
Larynx cutaway, looking down from above. The front of the larynx is at the top.
Epiglottis
This leaf-shaped flap of elastic cartilage forms the front edge of the laryngeal inlet, above the folds. It tips back over the inlet during swallowing.
Vestibular folds
These paired pink ridges sit above and farther out than the paler true vocal folds. They are also called false vocal folds.
True vocal folds
These pale folds sit below the vestibular folds. Their free inner edges border the glottic opening and vibrate to produce voice.
Glottic opening
This gap lies between the inner edges of the true vocal folds. It is wider toward the back in this view of the open airway.
Tracheal rings
Tracheal wall cutaway. The back wall is at the top of the exposed cross-section.
Back wall
This flexible back wall bridges the open ends of the cartilage rings. It contains the trachealis smooth muscle and faces the esophagus.
Tracheal lumen
This is the hollow air passage inside the trachea. The ring curves around its front and sides; the flexible back wall completes its boundary.
C-shaped cartilage
Stacked rings of hyaline cartilage support the front and sides of the trachea. Each ring is open at the back.
Inner lining
The exposed mucosa lines the air passage on the inside of the supporting cartilage. Microscopic cilia on its surface move mucus toward the throat.
Main bronchial split
Front view of the main bronchial split. The right side of the body is on the left of the image.
Lower trachea
Above the carina, the lower trachea is a single air passage. It continues into both main bronchi at the split.
Carina
This raised ridge inside the lower trachea separates the openings of the right and left main bronchi.
Right main bronchus
This branch on the left of the image leads to the right lung. It is typically wider, shorter, and more vertical than the left main bronchus.
Left main bronchus
This branch on the right of the image leads to the left lung. It is typically narrower, longer, and more oblique than the right main bronchus.
